body: I found this problem as well. After map_changed is received, call NavigationServer3D.map_get_closest_point always return 0,0,0

And that in fact, map_changed is always called twice.

and after second map_changed gets called, everything works

And I sugguest we add a NavigationServer3D.IsMapReady(rid) method to robustly check
because waiting for signal can raise race condition.

You are describing purely single-threaded behavior which was the case in Godot 4.4.
That is possible to achieve again by disabling the async iteration updates for regions and maps.
This was mentioned in the Godot version upgrade notes and PR notes as well as is mentioned in the documentation.

If you never change the navigation map after load you could use that to recreate the old behavior. If you do any changes to the navmesh at runtime expect performance issues without thread support enabled as the entire regions and map will sync at once on the main thread.

In general there is no idea of a "map ready" in async updates with threads as a map may sync but various region(s) may still run on thread tasks of various thread length or new may have started or just queued. There is no "I know I am done with everything" state there is only a "I am done with everything that I know about so far" state but that know-about might as well be nothing because everything was just queued up or running on thread tasks somewhere.

Closing this issue as the upgrade and change is documented and there are settings to control the behavior.

This issue shouldn't be closed. The problem still persists and no solution has been provided at all.

You can (and should) be able to track 'async' tasks precisely. It's harder, since you have to potentially communicate between threads, but it is not unfeasible by any means. I say 'async' in quotation marks because it is not even the right word to make that argument, since it could be async and not be running in parallel. This is also not well written in the documentation, which constantly assumes 'async' means having multiple threads running in parallel.

Why can't you have a `map_ready` signal in an async environment? The NavigationServer2D must have access to all the queued tasks, and know whether they have been finished or not. You make the argument that new work might be added, potentially making the ready state never achieved, but that is irrelevant as long as it is documented. For the majority of cases, it would suffice to be able to know whether the map is completely up to date or there are still pending changes that have not been applied.
